note: Editorial reads based on how these brands have been discounted in prior holiday seasons. Not a forecast or guarantee. 'match' strings are compared (case-insensitive) against each deal's brand and title.

brands.name: Target
brands.where: Toys, small appliances, TVs and home goods. See the calendar for its Early Black Friday window.
brands.trap: Target Circle member deals and Circle Card savings are conditional. Only the price everyone pays counts here.

brands.name: Nike
brands.where: Older colorways and last season's styles, on Nike.com and at sporting-goods stores.
brands.trap: “Extra % off sale styles” offers usually need a code or a member sign-in. That makes them conditional, so they don't count here.

brands.name: Pottery Barn
brands.where: Bedding, rugs, holiday décor and furniture across Pottery Barn, Pottery Barn Kids and Pottery Barn Teen.
brands.trap: Large furniture can add a delivery fee, and made-to-order pieces can take weeks. Compare the delivered price, not only the sale tag.

brands.name: Milwaukee
brands.where: Battery + charger starter kits and combo kits, especially at The Home Depot.
brands.trap: “Free tool with kit” promos aren’t a percent off. They only land here if the kit price itself drops 35%.

brands.name: Kohl's
brands.where: Small kitchen appliances, bedding, toys and apparel, with heavy doorbuster weeks around Black Friday.
brands.trap: Kohl's Cash is a reward on a future purchase, not a price drop, and percent-off codes are conditional. Only the posted sale price counts.

brands.name: Gap
brands.where: Gap, GapKids, babyGap, Gap Maternity, GapBody, GapFit and GapStudio, during frequent site-wide events.
brands.trap: Headline percentages often need a checkout code, or apply only to full-price styles. Check the item's own sale price.

brands.name: Crate & Barrel
brands.where: Cookware, dinnerware, small appliances and holiday décor, plus its CB2 and Crate & Kids lines.
brands.trap: Cookware sets are often put together for the sale. Price the pieces you'd actually use.

brands.name: LG
brands.where: OLED C-series TVs, plus refrigerators and laundry during appliance events.
brands.trap: Retailer-specific model codes can differ from the reviewed model. Match the full model number.

brands.name: LOFT
brands.where: Frequent site-wide percentage events, plus “extra % off sale” promotions.
brands.trap: The extra % comes off an already-reduced price and usually needs a code, which makes it conditional. Only the posted item price counts here.

brands.name: The North Face
brands.where: Past-season jackets and fleece at The North Face and outdoor and sporting-goods stores.
brands.trap: XPLR Pass member pricing is conditional. Colorway matters too: the discounted color is often not the one in the photo.

brands.name: Bass Pro Shops
brands.where: Outdoor apparel, coolers, fishing and camping gear at Bass Pro Shops and its sister chain Cabela's.
brands.trap: CLUB points and “bonus” gift cards aren't a price drop. Compare house brands like RedHead with similar gear from other brands.

brands.name: Best Buy
brands.where: TVs, laptops, headphones and appliances across its early, Black Friday and Cyber Monday events (see the calendar below).
brands.trap: Member-only prices and open-box listings are conditional or not new, so they don't count.

brands.name: Ann Taylor
brands.where: Suiting, sweaters and outerwear during seasonal events.
brands.trap: Promotions often exclude new arrivals and full-price suiting. Check the specific item, not the banner.

brands.name: Dick's Sporting Goods
brands.where: Past-season apparel and footwear, fitness equipment and outdoor gear, including Nike and The North Face.
brands.trap: ScoreCard member pricing and in-cart discounts are conditional. Only the posted shelf price counts.

brands.name: Disney / Pixar
brands.where: Toy Story 5 figures and playsets, especially at Target.
brands.trap: Character toys come in many near-identical sizes. Confirm the inch size and edition.

brands.name: Patagonia
brands.where: Patagonia doesn't run Black Friday sales on its own site. Markdowns show up at outdoor retailers, mostly on past-season colors.
brands.trap: Worn Wear (used gear) is cheaper, but it isn't a discount on a new item, so it never qualifies here.

brands.name: Hollister
brands.where: Site-wide and category events on jeans, hoodies, graphic tees and Gilly Hicks loungewear.
brands.trap: “Up to 50% off” covers a range. Check the individual item's own price pair, because many land well under the headline.

brands.name: Coach
brands.where: Coach's sale section, and Coach Outlet's near-constant markdowns.
brands.trap: Coach Outlet carries made-for-outlet styles. An outlet “was” price isn't the boutique price of a similar bag.

brands.name: Old Navy
brands.where: Doorbuster-priced basics: fleece, jeans, pajamas, kids' and baby, plus outlet locations.
brands.trap: Big “50% off” events can be measured against prices that are rarely charged. Use the lowest-price check in Deal Check below.

brands.name: Quince
brands.where: Low everyday prices. Occasional markdowns on discontinued colors.
brands.trap: Quince's “traditional retail” figure compares its price to other brands. It isn't Quince's own former price, so it never counts as a reference price here.

brands.name: DEWALT
brands.where: 20V MAX kits, oscillating and impact tools at Home Depot, Lowe’s and Amazon.
brands.trap: Same tool, different kit. Check battery Ah and what’s in the box before you compare prices.

brands.name: Samsung
brands.where: TVs, monitors, storage and kitchen appliances.
brands.trap: Doorbuster TVs can be derivative models with different panels or fewer ports than the flagship line.

brands.name: Athleta
brands.where: Leggings, outerwear and last season's colors in the sale section.
brands.trap: Athleta has no factory line. A deep cut here is usually a real markdown on a discontinued color or style.

brands.name: Banana Republic
brands.where: Sweaters, outerwear and suiting during seasonal events.
brands.trap: Promotions often exclude new arrivals and cashmere. Read the fine print on the specific item.

brands.name: Gap Factory
brands.where: Gap Factory and Gap Outlet stores and site, with deep percentage events through much of the year.
brands.trap: Gap Inc. describes its factory lines as “exclusively designed collections.” They aren't the same items as at Gap, so don't compare across stores.

brands.name: Banana Republic Factory
brands.where: Banana Republic Factory stores and site, with frequent site-wide percentage events.
brands.trap: Factory merchandise is made for the factory channel. Compare it to other factory prices, not to Banana Republic mainline.

brands.name: Sony
brands.where: Previous-generation headphones and TVs once newer models are out.
brands.trap: Current-generation flagships usually see smaller cuts than the older model sitting next to them.

brands.name: Apple
brands.where: Older AirPods models are the usual exception.
brands.trap: iPhone deals tied to carrier activation, trade-ins or gift cards don’t count. There’s no clean price pair.

brands.name: Dyson
brands.where: Cordless vacuums and hair tools, often sold as bundles.
brands.trap: Retailer-exclusive configurations exist. Compare the included attachments, not only the model name.

brands.name: KitchenAid
brands.where: Stand mixers and small kitchen appliances.
brands.trap: Holiday mixers are often a different series or bowl size than the one you priced in October.

brands.name: Ninja / Shark
brands.where: Air fryers, blenders, robot and stick vacuums.
brands.trap: Their reference prices move a lot during the year. A “was” price may be a recent high.

brands.name: LEGO
brands.where: Older sets at third-party stores like Target, Walmart and Amazon.
brands.trap: Brand-store promos lean on gifts with purchase and Insider points, which aren’t a price drop.

brands.name: Husky
brands.where: Hand tools, torque wrenches and mechanics sets, sold only at The Home Depot.
brands.trap: A store brand’s reference price is set by the store itself. Compare against similar sets from other brands.
